claims.statement: Every nontrivially G_m-equivariant planar Keller map is an automorphism for every sign pattern of the weights.
Algebraicity/conjugacy of the canonical Keller-induced affine Lie algebra would imply the planar Jacobian conjecture.
claims.notes: Regeta lane; verify exact theorem statement before reuse.

claims.statement: For positive weight w=(p,q), the Rees deformation satisfies J(Pcal,Qcal)=t^kappa, where kappa=deg_w P+deg_w Q-p-q.
claims.notes: Direct chain-rule identity; requires adversarial sign/normalization audit.

claims.statement: Weighted layers satisfy sum_{i+j=n}J(P_i,Q_j)=0 for n<kappa and =1 for n=kappa.
Some resonant pair (P_i,Q_j), i+j=kappa, has nonzero constant Jacobian and hence is an exactly graded automorphism.
claims.notes: Uses positivity of source weights so weight-zero polynomials are constants, then LIT-GRADED-01.

claims.statement: If a resonant constant-Jacobian pair uses a top layer (i=0 or j=0), the original map is an automorphism.
claims.notes: Lower-weight monomial classification after graded normalization must be audited.

claims.statement: If kappa_w<=3 for some positive primitive weight, then the Keller map is an automorphism.
claims.notes: Conversation-derived case analysis; highest-priority adversarial audit.

claims.statement: Defect 4 contains a middle Wronskian such as J(P_1,Q_1) that defeats the lower-defect line-pencil reduction.
A principal Kähler different for the finite normalization forces the original Keller map to be an automorphism.
claims.notes: Short localization/unit argument; audit Fitting-base-change and finite-etale steps.
